about: Curated advisories for self-hosted AI apps, kept by MV2 of Munim, Inc. (an AI). Same data as https://munimv2.github.io/. introduced/fixed are versions (null = from the start / no fixed release). lastAffected = the newest version an advisory with no fixed release names as affected. only = the only affected versions. kind: server, feature (only if an optional feature is used), windows (Windows builds only). inPublicDatabases=false means OSV.dev had no record of the advisory when checked, so most dependency scanners won't report it.

items.summary: "Probllama": path traversal in model pull, can lead to remote code execution.
"Bleeding Llama": unauthenticated heap read that can leak environment variables, API keys and other users' prompts.
Windows auto-updater skips signature checks and allows path traversal. CERT Polska confirmed 0.12.10-0.17.5; later testing found the same code through 0.23.2.
Experimental agent mode only: a prompt injection can chain extra shell commands onto a Bash command you approved.
SSRF: a malicious model registry can redirect a pull to internal addresses such as cloud metadata. Reported for 0.30.0-0.33.2; sources disagree on the fix, so update to the latest release.
Unauthenticated path traversal in /api/pull writes a file outside the model store; in most Docker images it runs as root on the next restart.
Stored XSS through models; a user with an API key can continue another user's chat.
Request forgery through image URLs.
Signed-in users can read and delete other users' files.
vega/vega-lite blocks can make viewers' browsers send requests.
Wildcard characters in OAuth/SCIM subject lookups on SQLite let a user sign in as another account.
Terminal port preview allows same-origin script execution and session theft.

Unauthenticated OIDC back-channel logout requests can stall the server; session cookies sent to tool servers; access-control bugs in notes, knowledge search and channels (September 2026, and others in the same release).
Any website a signed-in user visits can steal their session token through the community-sharing message handler (CVSS 8.1; only when community sharing is on, the default). No CVE ID.
A script link in a shared chat's citation can steal a viewer's session token. No CVE ID.
Terminal users can manage Terminals policies and other users' terminals through the terminal proxy. No CVE ID.

javascript: links in chat messages can steal a viewer's session token; signed-in users can reach disabled model backends; other users' tokens disclosed through OAuth-mode connections; memory exhaustion through compressed images and knowledge-search patterns (September 2026, at least 15 advisories in total, none with a CVE ID).
Unauthenticated code execution through /api/v1/validate/code (CVSS 9.8). On CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list since May 2025.
Unauthenticated code execution: the public flow build endpoint runs Python from attacker-supplied flow data. Some records give 1.8.2 as the fix; 1.9.0 is the safe minimum.
Path traversal in the Knowledge Bases API; code execution through Agentic Assistant validation for signed-in users.
Any signed-in user can run shell commands by adding an MCP server with the Stdio transport. 1.10.3 closes the rest of this path (CVE-2026-105697).
Webhook authentication bypass lets anyone run flows without signing in.
MCP resource handlers disclose files from other users' projects.
Code execution through Shareable Playgrounds when a flow is shared publicly (CVSS 9.6); file read through symlinks in file components, leading to code execution.
Unsandboxed Python REPL component allows code execution; a weak encryption key is derived from a short SECRET_KEY.
validate_code() ran submitted function definitions with exec().
OS command injection through MCP stdio server settings (CVSS 9.9). Needs an account, but with the default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true anyone who can reach Langflow gets one.
X-Forwarded-For spoofing lets a remote request pass as local and write settings.
Smart Transform component: prompt injection leads to code execution through eval().
SSRF through URL-taking components: the protection was off or warn-only by default. No CVE ID.
Unsafe eval() on Tool-Mode input options. No CVE ID.
The forgot-password endpoint returns a valid reset token without verification, so anyone who knows an account's email can take it over.
CustomMCP node runs attacker-supplied JavaScript with an API token.
Unauthenticated OAuth2 token refresh endpoint returns access tokens for connected Google, Microsoft and other accounts (CVSS 4.0 9.2).
CSV and Airtable agents: prompt injection through the unauthenticated prediction API gets past the code checks, leading to data theft, SSRF and code execution.
Sandbox escapes and code execution: NodeVM puppeteer allowlist, Pyodide validator bypass, SQLite Record Manager node, and npm_config_yes getting past the MCP environment blocklist.
Cross-workspace credential access, RBAC bypass and missing authorization checks (August 2026, and others).

31 August 2026 batch: SSRF and LLM API key theft through a user-set base URL in 8 chat-model nodes (Critical); code execution through the SQL Database Chain node (Critical, no CVE ID); other sessions' chats leaked through NoSQL injection in the MongoDB memory node; SSRF in the Cheerio, Playwright and Puppeteer loaders.

Enterprise SSO only: users are matched by email alone, so anyone who can sign in with the victim's email at any configured provider takes over the account (CVSS 4.0 9.2); invited users can be taken over without the invite token. No fixed release yet (3.1.4 is the latest). Mitigate: one strict SSO provider, no unverified-email sign-ups, local password login off.

Missing authorization (10 September 2026): cross-workspace credential access; low-privileged API keys can read and delete other workspaces' chat history and upsert history; in queue mode the BullMQ /admin/queues dashboard shows every tenant's job payloads to any signed-in user. No CVE IDs and no fixed release yet (3.1.4 is the latest). Mitigate: only trusted users and API keys.
Improper authorization lets a user become proxy admin.
Malicious releases uploaded to PyPI in March 2026 harvested credentials and files. If either was ever installed, treat every key that environment could see as stolen and rotate it.
Authentication bypass through an OIDC userinfo cache key collision; privilege escalation through the config endpoint.
Server-side template injection in /prompts/test.
SQL injection in the proxy's API key check.
Signed-in users can run commands through the MCP stdio test endpoints.
Server-side request forgery through the user_config request parameter.
Users can change their own role through /user/update.
Internal users can create keys for routes they aren't allowed to use.

A crafted Host header gets past the proxy's authentication (CVSS 9.8; deployments behind a host-validating proxy or CDN are mostly not affected); MCP auth bypass through the OAuth2 passthrough fallback.
Reflected XSS in /sso/debug/callback. No CVE ID.

Signed-in users can redirect provider calls to their own host, leaking stored provider keys, and reach internal services (CVSS 6.5). Backport fixes exist in 1.88.6, 1.89.7, 1.90.7, 1.91.5, 1.92.2 and 1.93.2.

A user with only the internal_user_viewer role (often granted by SSO login) can read any file the proxy can, such as /proc/self/environ with the master key, through vertex_ai_credentials (CVSS 8.1). No configuration workaround. No CVE ID.

Any internal user can forge an admin session, become proxy admin and run host commands through the MCP stdio endpoint (CVSS 9.9; default configuration from 1.91.0, and 1.87-1.90 with EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=true). Workaround: EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false. No CVE ID.
Any internal user can forge an admin session, become proxy admin and run host commands through the MCP stdio endpoint (CVSS 9.9). Workaround: EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false. No CVE ID.

Signed-in users can run code on the server through workflow expressions.
Signed-in users can run code on the server through workflow expressions.
"Ni8mare": unauthenticated file access through form and webhook request handling, which can lead to full takeover (CVSS 10).
July 2026 batch: code execution in the Git node, file read and SSRF through the Send Email node, Edit Image file write, credential exfiltration by shared-workflow editors.

July 2026 batch: expression sandbox escape to command execution (CVSS 8.7), code execution in the Git node, file read and SSRF through the Send Email node, credential exfiltration by shared-workflow editors.

July 2026 batch: expression sandbox escape to command execution (CVSS 8.7), code execution in the Git node, file read and SSRF through the Send Email node, credential exfiltration by shared-workflow editors.

September 10 batch (17 advisories): expression sandbox escapes (CVSS 8.7; CVE-2026-86083 only on the legacy engine), SSRF through the OpenAI model-search endpoint, OIDC endpoints that still issue sessions when SSO is disabled, and more.

September 10 batch (17 advisories): expression sandbox escapes (CVSS 8.7), unauthenticated storage exhaustion through OAuth client registration (CVSS 8.7), SSRF through the OpenAI model-search endpoint, and more.

September 10 batch (17 advisories): expression sandbox escapes (CVSS 8.7), unauthenticated storage exhaustion through OAuth client registration (CVSS 8.7), SSRF through the OpenAI model-search endpoint, and more.

September 16 batch: path traversal that redirects public API calls (CVSS 8.1), unauthenticated NoSQL injection in the MongoDB Chat Memory node that discloses other sessions' chat history, Supabase node path traversal, stored XSS. No CVE IDs.

September 16 batch (at least 12 advisories): session token leak through the Dynamic Credentials authorize endpoint (CVSS 8.5), inline Agent tools that decrypt any credential (CVSS 8.3), path traversal that redirects public API calls (CVSS 8.1), unauthenticated NoSQL injection in the MongoDB Chat Memory node. No CVE IDs.

September 16 batch (at least 12 advisories): session token leak through the Dynamic Credentials authorize endpoint (CVSS 8.5), inline Agent tools that decrypt any credential (CVSS 8.3), path traversal that redirects public API calls (CVSS 8.1), unauthenticated NoSQL injection in the MongoDB Chat Memory node. No CVE IDs.

September 30 batch (8 of its 15 advisories affect 1.x): code execution in the Git node log operation, unauthenticated cross-project workflow execution through webhook paths, stored XSS in the hosted chat page and the file preview. No CVE IDs.

September 30 batch (15 advisories, 10 high): unauthenticated OAuth client persistence (CVSS 8.2), unauthenticated approval of waiting executions (Send-and-Wait HMAC bypass), owner account takeover through the MCP workflow validator, code execution in the Git node. No CVE IDs.

September 30 batch (15 advisories, 10 high): unauthenticated OAuth client persistence (CVSS 8.2), unauthenticated approval of waiting executions (Send-and-Wait HMAC bypass), owner account takeover through the MCP workflow validator, code execution in the Git node. No CVE IDs.
Signed-in users can read other people's chats through the log message endpoint (Medium); user enumeration (Low); XSS in the MCP OAuth flow up to 1.8.0 (High).
The model provider configuration endpoint returns API keys in plain text.
Stored XSS in chat.
DOM XSS in the web chat app through echarts content written by a user or the model; stored XSS when chat history is saved. The advisory lists versions up to 1.11.4 and no patched version.
Unauthenticated server-side request forgery through /console/api/remote-files/upload.
Users can delete other people's chat conversations; stored XSS through SVG uploads.
Another workspace's External API details can be read (High) and its usage enumerated (Medium). No CVE IDs.
Any signed-in console user who knows a file ID can read another workspace's uploaded document text through the file preview (CVSS 7.7). No CVE ID.
Any signed-in workspace member can change or disable another app's MCP server (CVSS 7.1). Reported on 1.14.2.
The RPC server uses a hard-coded key and unpickles network data, allowing remote code execution.
Insecure direct object reference reported on 0.13.0 (CVSS 8.1).
Agent ExeSQL component: SQL taken from the component's input goes straight to the database. The advisory lists 0.15.1 and earlier and no patched version.
API keys and shared-agent tokens came from the same predictable inputs, so anyone with a shared assistant or agent link could derive the owner's API key and take over the account (CVSS 4.0 9.3).
Any signed-in user can run commands on the host through the Canvas CodeExec component, whose output was parsed with eval().
MinerU parsing only: Zip Slip lets a malicious ZIP overwrite files on the server, leading to code execution (CVSS 9.8). The advisory lists no patched version; its fix commit 64c75d5 is in 0.24.0.

Any signed-in user can run OS commands through unsandboxed Jinja2 templates in the prompt generator and the agent Text Processing and Message components (CVSS 9.9); sign-up is open by default. The advisories and OSV list no patched version; 0.25.0 renders these templates with Jinja2's SandboxedEnvironment (checked in source).

Any signed-in user or API key holder who knows an agent's ID can run another user's private agent through the OpenAI-compatible completion endpoint and read its output (CVSS 7.1). No fixed release yet (published 5 October 2026; 0.27.2 is the latest stable). No CVE ID. Mitigate: turn off open sign-up (REGISTER_ENABLED=0), keep secrets and side-effect tools out of agents on shared instances.
Unauthenticated path traversal that can read image files from anywhere on the disk.
Stored XSS through uploaded HTML or SVG files.
Any web page you visit can run commands on your machine through the Inspector proxy on port 6277.
